guidance: Dimensional reference only: the table gives the key section and the two keyway depths for a nominal shaft diameter. It does not size the key for the torque the joint has to carry, and it does not check the shaft, hub or key material, so take the strength from the drive design. Check the standard sheet or the key supplier for the width and depth tolerances before cutting.
method: DIN 6885-1 parallel keys, chosen by the nominal shaft diameter. The table is a band lookup: each row covers shafts from just above its lower bound up to and including its upper bound (over 6 to 8, over 8 to 10, through over 440 to 500 mm), so a 30 mm shaft stays in the 22-30 mm band with an 8 x 7 mm key while a 30.01 mm shaft moves to 10 x 8 mm. Each row gives the key width b, its height h, the keyway depth in the shaft and the keyway depth in the hub, all in millimetres; the depth in the shaft is the larger of the two above about 22 mm, because the shaft slot takes the key and the hub slot only clears it. Vendor copies of the standard label those two depths t1 and t2 in opposite orders, so the page names them by where they are cut instead. The shop measurements follow directly: the shaft slot reads d - (depth in shaft) from the bottom of the keyway to the opposite outside diameter, and the hub slot reads d + (depth in the hub) from the bottom of the keyway to the opposite side of the bore. The key cross-section is b x h, and the keyway width is normally N9 in the shaft and JS9 in the hub, with P9 as the fixed fit. Inch diameters are converted at 25.4 mm to choose the band and both values are shown. Values are shown to at most three decimals. Everything is computed in the browser; nothing is stored, uploaded or fetched.
